patch.value: Bounded activity and context reads still parse every entry of each stream their window reaches, so one long-lived stream with a single recent event costs its whole history

Raised by the Codex review of the pm-gh1664 change on 2026-11-20. The derived stream summary (runtime/history-stream-summary.json) lets pm activity and the pm context activity section skip whole streams that cannot reach their window, but a stream that does reach it is parsed from the first entry: an item with years of history and one event in the default 24-hour digest window, or one that supplies a top-three context row, costs its complete stream on every read, and adding archive depth to active streams slows both commands without changing their output. The scale benchmark (scripts/bench/history-read-costs.mjs) spreads archive depth across 2,000 streams and does not exercise this shape. Bounding inside a stream needs a suffix read from a recorded byte offset whose prefix is proven unchanged: an append keeps the inode and grows the file, but an in-place rewrite that keeps or grows the size defeats a size-only check, so the offset needs a verified boundary (for example the recorded line's after_hash at that offset plus the inode) and a full read whenever the boundary does not verify. Duplicate check: searched intra-stream, tail read, suffix offset, long-lived stream and bounded activity; pm-gh1679 owns backwards paging of one item's history (a producer cursor), pm-29ymfn verified-prefix receipts for strict verification, neither the activity window read.

A bounded activity or context read of a stream with a verified recorded boundary parses only the entries after that boundary that can reach the window, and falls back to the full stream when the boundary does not verify; Output is identical to the complete read, proven by a spec with a stream rewritten in place at equal and larger size; The history read benchmark gains a long-lived-stream fixture whose bounded p50 stays independent of that stream's depth
An activity read costs the entries that can reach its window, even inside a long-lived stream
A stream that reaches the window is parsed in full
